page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Dadv6 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware allocation includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 236 GB local disk and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU resources are included.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. However, multi-core execution and memory write bandwidth fall into the average range. The instance exhibits performance trade-offs in memory read bandwidth, both cached and uncached, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which rank in the bottom 25%. Database operations and software compilation tasks also show weaker relative performance, while LLM inference with a medium 7B model is poor to weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ads_v6 offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB RAM per vCPU alongside bundled local storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without the premium cost of memory-optimized hardware. The instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, Redis caching, and moderate single-threaded processing tasks. It is less suitable for memory-bandwidth-intensive applications, large-scale database operations, or heavy multi-threaded compilation.
